operator.heading: 1. Operator & controller

privacy.heading: 2. Privacy notice under Art. 13 GDPR
privacy.introBefore: Your privacy and data sovereignty come first. Only the technical minimum needed for reliable chat, voice and video is collected. Your data is
privacy.introStrong: never sold, never passed on to advertisers and never used to train AI models
privacy.basisConsent: : By registering and using your invite code you consent to your profile data and uploaded media being stored.
privacy.basisContractTitle: Performance of a contract / terms of use (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR)
privacy.basisContract: : To provide the chat and voice service, authentication and session management.
privacy.basisInterest: : Short-lived error and access logs to protect against abuse and brute-force attacks.
privacy.voiceHeading: WebRTC voice, video & screen sharing: 100% routed through the server
privacy.voiceBefore: Unlike typical chat apps, Mnema Talk runs a dedicated
privacy.voiceNoP2p: There are no direct peer-to-peer connections between participants.
privacy.voiceAfter1: Your IP address is therefore never disclosed to other people in a Talk. Audio streams and screen shares are forwarded selectively in real time in memory and
privacy.voiceNoRecord: are never recorded or stored permanently
privacy.stunBefore: To set up the voice connection, your browser asks the following STUN servers for your public address:
privacy.stunAfter: . Your IP address is sent to the operator of each of these servers; no conversation or message content is transmitted.
privacy.updateCheck: About every 30 minutes the server asks GitHub (api.github.com, GitHub Inc., USA) whether a new version of Mnema Talk was released. GitHub only sees the server’s IP address; no user data is sent. The operator can turn the check off.
privacy.turnBefore: If your network blocks the direct media connection, your browser can relay it through the following TURN servers configured by the operator:
privacy.turnAfter: . The operator of each of these servers receives your IP address and port and passes on the encrypted media, which the server cannot read; no conversation or message content is transmitted.
privacy.builtinTurn: Members on restrictive networks can reach voice and video through a relay that runs inside this server. It is part of this server and operated by the operator of this instance, not by a third party, and it forwards media only to the server’s own media server. The relay sees your IP address and port and passes on the encrypted media (DTLS-SRTP), which it cannot read. It uses short-lived credentials tied to your account and stores nothing persistently: it keeps only operational counters (active sessions, refused attempts, traffic totals) without IP addresses or account names, and writes IP addresses and account IDs to the log only when the operator turns on debug logging. Purpose and legal basis are those of the voice service above (contract, Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR).
privacy.noStun: No external STUN or TURN servers from third parties are used.
privacy.mediaPurpose: Images, documents and avatars in the local S3 storage
privacy.sessionRetention: Up to {days} days or until you sign out
privacy.moderationPurpose: Reports, automod entries and private notes that moderators keep about members; never part of a data export
privacy.moderationRetention: Until the moderators delete them; entries about a deleted account stay under “Deleted member”
privacy.rightsHeading: Your rights as a data subject
privacy.rights1Before: Under Art. 15–22 GDPR you have the right at any time, free of charge, to
privacy.rights1Mid5: . To exercise these rights, simply email
privacy.rights2Before: You may also object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21 GDPR) and withdraw any consent you gave at any time with effect for the future (Art. 7(3) GDPR). You also have the right to
privacy.rightsComplain: lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority

privacy.noiseFilter: AI noise suppression (DeepFilterNet3 or GTCRN) runs entirely in your browser. Your microphone signal is not sent to any third party for it; the model and code come from this server.
privacy.selfService: Without emailing anyone: under Account & security in the account menu you can download a copy of your data (JSON files in a ZIP, once per day) and delete your account yourself. Deleting erases your profile, avatar, e-mail address, sessions and uploads; your messages stay in their threads as written by “Deleted member” without their text. An optional e-mail address is used only to confirm it and to reset your password, and is never shown to other members.
privacy.addressDetection: When the operator has not set the server’s public address, the server sends one STUN request at startup (and about every 10 minutes) to Google (stun.l.google.com, Google LLC, USA) or Cloudflare (stun.cloudflare.com, Cloudflare Inc., USA) to learn its own address for voice. They only see the server’s IP address; no user data is sent. The operator can turn this off.
privacy.clockCheck: About every 6 hours the server asks an NTP time server (time.cloudflare.com, Cloudflare Inc., USA, or pool.ntp.org) for the time to check its own clock. They only see the server’s IP address; no user data is sent. The operator can turn this off.

trusted_proxy_broad.title: TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS is too broad
trusted_proxy_broad.body: It contains broad ranges while the server is reachable beyond loopback. Any host in those ranges can forge its client address and evade rate limits and the sign-in lock. List only your reverse proxy’s address.

proxy_not_trusted.title: Requests arrive through an untrusted proxy
proxy_not_trusted.body: Requests came in through a proxy that is not in TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS, so all clients share one rate-limit identity. Add the reverse proxy’s address to TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS.

webrtc_udp_mux_disabled.title: Voice capacity is limited

insecure_public_url.title: PUBLIC_URL is not https
insecure_public_url.body: Session cookies are sent without the Secure flag and the __Host- prefix, so someone on the network path can read or replace them. Set PUBLIC_URL to the https:// address people open, behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS.

ok.detail: The server clock is within {window} of real time.

skewed.detail: The server clock is off by about {skew}, which breaks two-factor codes and session expiry.
skewed.fix: Turn on time synchronization (NTP) on the host; on a Synology: Control Panel > Regional Options > Time > Synchronize with an NTP server.

unreachable.fix: Check that the postgres container is healthy (docker compose ps) and that POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env is the one it was created with.

none.detail: No outgoing mail: members get no reset link for a forgotten login and e-mail addresses cannot be confirmed.
none.fix: Optional: set SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD and SMTP_FROM in .env.

address_mismatch.detail: This host’s own address {local} differs from the address {public} the internet sees, so its traffic leaves through another gateway and announcing {public} may be wrong.
address_mismatch.fix: If this host is reachable from outside on {local}, set WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP={local}; if a router or gateway sits in front, forward the voice ports there.

cgnat.detail: This home connection has no public IPv4 address of its own (the address {address} is in the carrier-grade NAT range 100.64.0.0/10), so port forwarding cannot work and members outside your network cannot reach voice.
cgnat.fix: Home connection without own public IPv4 - port forwarding cannot work. Options: ask the internet provider for a public IPv4 address, run Mnema Talk on a VPS, or use an external relay (WEBRTC_TURN_URLS and WEBRTC_TURN_SECRET). See “Can I host at home?” in doc/operations.md.

no_ipv4.detail: No public IPv4 address was found but IPv6 works: this looks like a connection without its own public IPv4 (DS-Lite), so port forwarding cannot work and members outside your network cannot reach voice over IPv4.
no_ipv4.fix: Home connection without own public IPv4 - port forwarding cannot work. Options: ask the internet provider for a public IPv4 address, run Mnema Talk on a VPS, or use an external relay (WEBRTC_TURN_URLS and WEBRTC_TURN_SECRET). See “Can I host at home?” in doc/operations.md.

insecure.detail: PUBLIC_URL is plain http://, so session cookies lose the Secure flag and the __Host- prefix.
insecure.fix: Put a reverse proxy with TLS in front and set PUBLIC_URL=https://chat.example.com (skip this on a trusted LAN).

local.detail: PUBLIC_URL is {public_url}, which only this machine can open; invite links, e-mails and browser origin checks use it. That is fine for trying Mnema Talk on this computer, but nobody else can join.
local.fix: To invite others, set PUBLIC_URL=https://chat.example.com (the address members type into their browser) in .env and run docker compose up -d.

origin_mismatch.detail: You opened this page at {origin} but PUBLIC_URL is {public_url}.
origin_mismatch.fix: If {origin} is the address members use, set PUBLIC_URL={origin}; if you came through a reverse proxy, let it pass the Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers.

broad.detail: TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS covers a wide range, so any host in it can forge a client address.
broad.fix: List only the reverse proxy’s own address in TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS.

not_trusted.detail: Requests arrive with X-Forwarded-For from a proxy that is not trusted, so every member looks like one address to rate limits and the login lockout.
not_trusted.fix: Set TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS=<address of your reverse proxy> in .env (its container IP, the Docker bridge gateway or its LAN address; never a whole private range).

not_configured.detail: Object storage is not configured, so uploads and avatars do not work.
not_configured.fix: Set S3_ENDPOINT, S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY and S3_SECRET_KEY in .env.

unreachable.detail: Object storage does not answer yet; uploads fail until it does.
unreachable.fix: Check that the seaweedfs container is running (docker compose ps) and that S3_ACCESS_KEY and S3_SECRET_KEY in .env match the ones it was first started with.

builtin_failed.detail: The built-in TURN relay could not listen on port {port}: another program on this host is probably using it, so members on networks that block UDP cannot join voice.
builtin_failed.fix: Stop whatever uses port {port} (UDP and TCP) or pick another port with WEBRTC_BUILTIN_TURN_PORT (and forward that one), then run docker compose up -d.

builtin_failed_external.detail: A TURN relay is configured for members behind strict firewalls; the built-in relay could not start.

builtin_off_external.detail: A TURN relay is configured for members behind strict firewalls; the built-in relay is not running.

builtin_ok.detail: The built-in TURN relay serves members behind strict firewalls on port {port}; forward it (UDP and TCP) next to the voice ports.

external_ok.detail: A TURN relay is configured for members behind strict firewalls.

none.detail: No TURN relay: members on networks that block UDP cannot join voice.
none.fix: Optional: remove WEBRTC_BUILTIN_TURN=off to use the built-in relay (forward port {port}, UDP and TCP), or set WEBRTC_TURN_URLS and WEBRTC_TURN_SECRET for an external one.

unreachable.detail: The built-in TURN relay runs, but this server could not verify port {port} from the inside; a router without NAT loopback causes this although the forward works.
unreachable.fix: Open Test my connection from a phone on mobile data to check the relay from outside; if it fails, forward port {port} (UDP and TCP) to this server, or set WEBRTC_BUILTIN_TURN_HOST if members must reach it under another name.

voice_unavailable.detail: The built-in TURN relay is not running because voice is unavailable: members on networks that block UDP cannot join voice.
voice_unavailable.fix: Fix the voice engine first (see the Voice port check), then run docker compose up -d.

announced_public_url.detail: Voice is announced on {ips} (taken from PUBLIC_URL).

announced_stun.detail: Voice is announced on {ips} (detected with a STUN request).

development.detail: Development mode: voice uses this machine’s own addresses.

missing.detail: No public voice address is known, so browsers are told the container’s own address.
missing.fix: Set WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP=<your public IPv4 address or dynamic-DNS name> in .env (add the LAN address after a comma for members on the same network), then docker compose up -d.

missing_detect_failed.detail: No public voice address is known, so browsers are told the container’s own address. Automatic detection failed: {error}.
missing_detect_failed.fix: Set WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP=<your public IPv4 address or dynamic-DNS name> in .env (add the LAN address after a comma for members on the same network), then docker compose up -d.

missing_detect_failed_turn_only.detail: No public voice address is known, so browsers are told the container’s own address. Automatic detection failed: {error}. Only the TURN relay can carry voice.
missing_detect_failed_turn_only.fix: Set WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP=<your public IPv4 address or dynamic-DNS name> in .env (add the LAN address after a comma for members on the same network), then docker compose up -d.

missing_turn_only.detail: No public voice address is known, so browsers are told the container’s own address. Only the TURN relay can carry voice.
missing_turn_only.fix: Set WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP=<your public IPv4 address or dynamic-DNS name> in .env (add the LAN address after a comma for members on the same network), then docker compose up -d.

unconfirmed.detail: Listening – not yet confirmed from outside. Voice listens on UDP {port}, but no member from outside this network has connected since the server started, so the router forward is unproven.
unconfirmed.fix: Forward UDP {port_min}-{port_max} from the router to this host, then open Test my connection from a phone on mobile data (Wi-Fi off); this turns green once it works.

confirmed.detail: Confirmed: a member from outside connected ({time}). Voice listens on UDP {port}.

mux_disabled.detail: WEBRTC_UDP_MUX_PORT=0 gives every media peer its own port, which caps how many people can be in calls.
mux_disabled.fix: Remove WEBRTC_UDP_MUX_PORT (or set it to {port_min}) so all peers share one UDP port.

unavailable.detail: The voice engine did not start, so Talks have no audio or video.
unavailable.fix: Another program may be using UDP ports {port_min}-{port_max} on the host: stop it or change WEBRTC_UDP_PORT_MIN and WEBRTC_UDP_PORT_MAX, then restart; the log names the cause.

ok.detail: WebSocket via proxy OK: a browser opened /api/ws and it upgraded ({time}).

unchecked.detail: Not checked yet: no browser has opened the live connection (/api/ws) since the server started.
unchecked.fix: Reload this page; if it stays unchecked, enable WebSocket in your reverse proxy.

failing.detail: Browsers tried to open /api/ws {count} times without a WebSocket upgrade (last {time}); the reverse proxy most likely does not pass WebSocket connections, so the app shows “Connection lost”.
failing.fix: Enable WebSocket in your reverse proxy: it must pass the headers Upgrade: websocket and Connection: Upgrade. Nginx Proxy Manager: switch on Websockets Support. nginx: proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection upgrade; proxy_http_version 1.1. Caddy and Traefik do this by default.

connectionTest.title: Test my connection
connectionTest.intro: Checks from this device whether voice can reach the server: directly over UDP and through the built-in relay. It needs no microphone and does not join a Talk.

step.speed: Measuring the download from the server…

verdict.relay_only: Only the relay works (direct UDP blocked or not forwarded)

ok.text: This device reached the voice port directly over UDP.

same_network.text: This device seems to be on the same network as the server, so this says little about the way in from outside.
same_network.fix: Run the test again from a phone on mobile data (Wi-Fi off).

udp_not_forwarded.text: The relay answers, but direct UDP to the voice port does not arrive. Most likely the router does not forward the voice ports, a firewall blocks them, or the announced address is wrong.
udp_not_forwarded.fix: Forward the voice UDP ports (50000-50050 by default) from the router to the server, open them in the host firewall, and check WEBRTC_NAT_1TO1_IP.

udp_blocked.text: Only the relay over TCP works: this network blocks UDP. That is common in company networks and with some VPNs.
udp_blocked.fix: Calls work through the relay. For better quality try another network or switch off the VPN.

voice_off.text: The voice engine of the server is not running.
voice_off.fix: An administrator should open Admin > Status and fix the Voice port item; the server log names the cause.

no_relay_offered.text: Direct UDP does not work and the server offers no TURN relay as a fallback.
no_relay_offered.fix: Turn the built-in relay on (remove WEBRTC_BUILTIN_TURN=off), forward its port 3479 (UDP and TCP) and forward the voice UDP ports.

only_local_addresses.text: This device found only local addresses: neither the STUN nor the relay servers answered. A firewall, a VPN or a browser privacy setting blocks UDP and the relay ports.
only_local_addresses.fix: Try another network or switch off the VPN or WebRTC protection. On the server, forward port 3479 (UDP and TCP).

relay_unreachable.text: The relay did not answer on any route, and direct UDP does not work either.
relay_unreachable.fix: Forward the relay port (3479 by default) for UDP and TCP to the server and check that Admin > Status shows the TURN relay as running.

limited.text: Too many tests in a row.
limited.fix: Wait a few minutes and run the test again.

ok.one: Your device downloaded from the server at {mbps} Mbit/s, measured to where the server is reachable (the nearest reverse proxy or tunnel). That is roughly its upload: enough for a screen share watched by about {count} member ({rate} Mbit/s plus {overhead} % overhead each). A short test; your own connection can be the limit.
